newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank ups H1 pre-tax profit 23 pct.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank ups H1 pre-tax profit 23 pct.

text.p: Britain's Royal Bank of Scotland on Wednesday reported a 23 percent increase in first half pre-tax profits and said progress in developing new and existing businesses gave a firm foundation for the group to move forward.

Pre-tax profit of 369 million pounds was within analysts' expectations and compared with 301 million pounds for the same period the previous year. The bank said it would pay an interim dividend of 6.2 pence per share, up from 5.4 pence.

"The record profits achieved in the first half...and the excellent progress made in developing both existing and new businesses provide a firm foundation from which the group can move forward with confidence," Royal Bank's chairman Lord Younger said in a statement.

Royal Bank said the results reflected a strong performance in British banking, which saw pre-tax profits rise 24 percent by 60 million pounds ($98.1 million) and its cost/income ratio improve by four percentage points. Corporate and instituational banking contributed 179 million pounds profit.

But provisions for bad and doubtful debts were 32 million pounds higher at 77 million pounds. Provisions for U.S. retail banking unit Citizens Financial were 23 percent higher while in British banking they increased by 18 million to 68 million pounds "as a result of formula driven provisions on the increased credit card balances and reduced recoveries and releases".

The Direct Line Insurance operation showed a small increase in profits for the half year to March 31 of eight million pound from five million pounds in the same period a year earlier. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
